gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the two built-in preamps' LINE outputs side by side. Audio-Technica's 36 dB stage raises 4.0 mV to 252 mV (-12 dBV) on the AT-LP70XBT. The Fluance RT81's preamp gives 140 mV, about 5 dB quieter into the same powered-speaker AUX input, and Home Theater HiFi's John E. Johnson, Jr. listed 'higher output (0.5 volts)' among his wishes for it.
standout_why: I compared against platterandplinth.com, valveandvinyl.com, stylusandsound.com and fewbetter.com. Platterandplinth explains the double-preamp mistake (a LINE deck into a PHONO input) and the 'one preamp in the chain' rule, but gives no numbers. Valveandvinyl gives the AT decks' '36 dB nominal gain' and the RT81's true bypass, but no mV output. Stylusandsound gives the RT81+ as '4.0 mV phono output and a 140 mV line output' but nothing for the AT or Sony decks. Fewbetter has no turntable content at all. None of them compares the two LINE levels or puts a dB figure on the double-preamp overload. The parts exist across rival pages, so the new part is the comparison.
decides: This confirms the plan works on every candidate. Each one has a PHONO/LINE selector, so the shopper sets LINE for powered speakers or an AUX input and PHONO only when feeding a receiver's PHONO jack. It also tilts the pick slightly. Into the same powered speakers, the AT-LP70X/LP70XBT gives about 5 dB more drive than the RT81 (252 vs 140 mV). That matters with low-sensitivity speakers or Bluetooth speakers that have a weak AUX input. The RT81 suits someone planning an external phono stage, because its PHONO setting bypasses the electronics. Wrongly plugging 252 mV into a PHONO input that expects about 4 mV overdrives it by about 36 dB, which is the distortion the rivals only describe in words.

findings.label: Phono pre-amp gain

findings.note: Checks out: 4.0 mV × 10^(36/20) = 4.0 × 63.1 ≈ 252 mV. Plugging LINE into an amplifier's PHONO input therefore feeds it about 36 dB (63×) more than the roughly 4 mV it expects, and the signal is RIAA-equalized a second time.

findings.source_title: Fluance RT81 Turntable, Cartridge, and Phono Preamplifier Review – Secrets of Home Theater and High Fidelity
findings.note: The review's spec box says 'PHONO OUTPUT: 140 mV'. That is the preamp's output, since the AT95E cartridge alone is single-digit mV. Reviewer John E. Johnson, Jr. lists 'Higher output (0.5 volts) from the phono preamplifier' as a wish and says the rear panel 'allows you to use either the phono preamplifier output or the cartridge output'. Stylusandsound (a rival) gives the same 140 mV for the RT81+.
